land.text: Prome and the Irrawaddy country 'up to Tharrawaddy and Myede', seized from Ava by Thado Minsaw after Mingyi Swa's death in 1482

predecessors.note: The Prome page gives the year only through its 1482-1542 header and the death of the governor Mingyi Swa in 1482; the ava-kingdom dossier carries the matching loss.

land.text: Prome and its district, surrendered by Minkhaung on 19 May 1542

successors.note: The page gives the Toungoo conquest in 1542; Cliopatria keeps the Prome row to 1546. The shan-states dossier carries the same land as Confederation territory from 1533 (see notes).

capitals.name: Prome (Pyay)
capitals.note: The page says the kingdom was based in Prome (Pyay); the infobox has no capital field.

rulers.name: Thado Minsaw
rulers.note: Governor of Tharrawaddy who 'seized Prome and declared himself king'; 'Thado Minsaw died in 1526'. The infobox gives four unlabelled ruler periods (1482-1526, 1526-1532, 1532-1539, 1539-1542); the names are matched to them from the text.

rulers.name: Bayin Htwe
rulers.note: 'succeeded by his son Bayin Htwe' in 1526; shut out by his son Narapati in 1532.

rulers.name: Narapati
rulers.note: 'Bayin Htwe's son Narapati shut the gates against his father' (1532); his regnal years are not on the page, so 1539 is the infobox period boundary.

rulers.name: Minkhaung (of Prome)
rulers.note: 'Narapati too died soon after and was succeeded by Minkhaung'; surrendered on 19 May 1542. Not the Minkhaung II of Ava.

keyframe_review.note: 18,965 km2 for 1482-1501. The page says Prome 'became an independent kingdom with territories up to Tharrawaddy and Myede' (no year); the shape's bounding box (17.64-19.64 N, 94.83-96.65 E) runs from the Tharrawaddy latitude to the Myede (Aunglan) latitude, so the extent agrees. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

19,356 km2 for 1502-1539, within 2 percent of 1482. The pages give no border change for these decades: Prome was Ava's ally against the Confederation until the 1520s, an ally of the Confederation in 1525 and 'a tributary of the Confederation in 1532'. The tributary status is not drawn as a loss here (see notes).

correction.text: the same outline, but for 1540-1542 only: Minkhaung surrendered Prome to Toungoo on 19 May 1542 and the kingdom ends there

keyframe_review.note: 19,580 km2. Cliopatria keeps the Prome row to 1546; the page has the siege begin in late 1541 and the kingdom fall on 19 May 1542 ('the small kingdom fell to the Toungoo forces in 1542'). The shape is unchanged; only its last year is 1542, and the Prome land is Toungoo's from May 1542 (first-toungoo-empire ledger).

region.text: Prome and the country up to Tharrawaddy and Myede

ledger.note: 1482: Thado Minsaw makes Prome a kingdom. 'Thado Minsaw seized Prome and declared himself king' after the governor Mingyi Swa 'died in 1482'; the page header reads 1482-1542 and the seizure itself carries no year in the text. Ava could not retake it: the Yamethin and Shan rebellions 'consumed its resources for the next two decades'.

region.text: Prome, attacked by the Confederation's forces

ledger.note: 1532: the Confederation of Shan States comes down on its former ally. 'In 1532, the Confederation forces came down and attacked Prome.'

1532: Prome becomes the Confederation's tributary and keeps its king. 'Prome itself became a tributary of the Confederation in 1532' and the infobox status reads 'Kingdom, vassal of Shan states (1532-1542)'; the First Toungoo Empire page has the Confederation 'by 1533 ... defeated its erstwhile ally Prome'. The shan-states dossier draws this as an annexation in 1533; this page keeps the Prome kings (Narapati, then Minkhaung) to 1542, so the land is a vassal tint, not a loss.

Late 1541: Toungoo besieges Prome. 'In late 1541, Toungoo again laid siege to Prome' after Prome sheltered fleeing Hanthawaddy troops in 1539 ('Narapati provided shelter to the fleeing Hanthawaddy troops in 1539').
19 May 1542: the siege ends in surrender. 'On 19 May 1542 (5th waxing of Nayon 904 ME), Minkhaung surrendered.'

19 May 1542: Prome passes to Toungoo. 'the small kingdom fell to the Toungoo (Taungoo) forces in 1542'; it rose again in revolt in May 1550 (put down August 1551) and in 1594-1608, 're-annexed by King Anaukpetlun in July 1608'.
1542: the Prome Kingdom ends. Minkhaung surrendered on 19 May 1542; the page's header closes the kingdom at 1542 and Cliopatria's four extra years (to 1546) are not supported.

wars.name: Confederation of Shan States attack on Prome

zones.text: Prome, attacked by the Confederation's forces in 1532

wars.outcome: Prome becomes a tributary of the Confederation (infobox: 'vassal of Shan states (1532-1542)') and keeps its own kings.
wars.note: Prome had been the Confederation's ally against Ava in the 1520s (the combined armies sacked Ava in March 1525; the Confederation took Ava on 25 March 1527). The zone is the 1532 contest region (the whole kingdom, 'In 1532, the Confederation forces came down and attacked Prome'); no border moved.

wars.name: Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War
wars.outcome: Toungoo conquers Hanthawaddy by 1541; Prome, which had sheltered Hanthawaddy troops in 1539, is besieged in late 1541 and surrenders on 19 May 1542.
wars.note: 'In the late 1530s, Prome became ensnarled in the Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War (1534-1541).' Prome's own part is the siege below.

wars.name: Toungoo siege of Prome
wars.outcome: Minkhaung of Prome surrenders on 19 May 1542; the kingdom ends.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes the Prome frontier: the page gives 'territories up to Tharrawaddy and Myede' and no boundary, and Cliopatria's three outlines differ by under 3 percent.

sources.title: Prome Kingdom
sources.note: Identity, 1482 origin, rulers, the 1532 tributary status, the 1541-42 siege and the 19 May 1542 surrender; read twice with two prompts. The infobox gives no area and no capital.

notes:
Page budget 1-2: one page opened (Prome Kingdom); the First Toungoo Empire page opened for the first-toungoo-empire dossier carries the same facts (Prome sidebar 1482-1542) and was not needed here.

Cliopatria's row 1482-1546 is one state; its last four years (1543-1546) follow the fall of the kingdom on 19 May 1542 and are not supported: the first-toungoo-empire dossier draws the Prome land from 1542. Cliopatria's Toungoo 1547 shape then contains all 66 Prome cells.

Conflict with the shan-states dossier (another group): it records a gain from prome-kingdom in 1533 and a loss to first-toungoo-empire in 1542, i.e. Prome as Confederation territory. This page says Prome 'became a tributary of the Confederation in 1532' (infobox 'Kingdom, vassal of Shan states (1532-1542)') and keeps its own kings, so the faithful record is vassal_start/vassal_end 1532-1542 in the shan-states ledger (counterpart prome-kingdom) with the land still Prome's; no loss is written here. The two dossiers should be reconciled by the gap-filler: either shan-states switches to vassal events, or this ledger gains a 1532 loss to shan-states and the 1542 loss moves to the Shan side.

Not settled: the year of Thado Minsaw's seizure (page header 1482; text silent); Narapati's and Minkhaung's regnal years (infobox periods used); the Prome alliance with Mingyi Nyo of Toungoo in 1504 (First Toungoo Empire page, ambiguous who defeated whose raids in 1504-05 and 1507-08) is not drawn. Later history: revolt of Thado Dhamma Yaza I (May 1550 to August 1551) and of 1594-1608, re-annexed by Anaukpetlun in July 1608: these belong to first-toungoo-empire.
